title: Mini Servo Radar
tagline: A modular Arduino-based radar system with automatic and manual scanning modes, visualized in real time using Processing.
problem: I wanted to build more than a basic Arduino sensor project. The goal was to create a modular embedded system that combined sensing, actuation, user input, and a real-time visualization interface while practicing clean project organization and hardware abstraction.

components.name: Arduino Uno
components.purpose: Main microcontroller that controls the entire system.

components.name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Sensor
components.purpose: Measures object distance during each scan.

components.name: SG90 Servo Motor
components.purpose: Rotates the ultrasonic sensor through a 180° sweep.

components.name: 10k Potentiometer
components.purpose: Provides manual control of the servo angle.

components.name: Toggle Switch
components.purpose: Switches between automatic and manual scanning modes.

timeline.title: Servo Control
timeline.desc: Implemented smooth 180° automatic servo sweep using modular servo control functions.

timeline.title: Distance Measurement
timeline.desc: Integrated the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor and displayed live angle and distance data through Serial Monitor.

timeline.title: Radar Visualization
timeline.desc: Developed a Processing application that receives serial data and renders a real-time semicircular radar interface.

timeline.title: Manual Control
timeline.desc: Added potentiometer-based manual scanning and implemented mode switching using a toggle switch.

timeline.title: Project Organization
timeline.desc: Refactored the project into separate modules for servo control, ultrasonic sensing, and user input, then documented and published it on GitHub.

failures: Initially planned to use a 16x2 LCD but replaced it with a Processing-based radar interface for a more informative visualization.
Experienced unstable ultrasonic readings while the servo was moving, which was improved by adding a short stabilization delay before measurements.
Encountered serial communication issues while integrating Processing and resolved them by using a consistent CSV data format and matching baud rates.

reflections.what_worked: Separating the firmware into independent modules made development, testing, and debugging significantly easier. Using Processing instead of an LCD produced a much clearer and more engaging visualization of the sensor data.
reflections.what_failed: The original plan of displaying information on a 16x2 LCD limited the user experience and provided little insight into the scanning process, so it was replaced with a graphical interface.
reflections.next_time: Replace delay-based timing with millis() for non-blocking operation, add object persistence and radar sweep trails, apply distance filtering for smoother measurements, and migrate the project to an ESP32 or STM32 platform with a standalone graphical display.
